whenToBringYourOwn: You want your own brand on the Google consent screen instead of Composio's.
You need restricted scopes (gmail.readonly, gmail.modify, mail.google.com) beyond Composio's defaults.
You need a dedicated Gmail API quota rather than sharing Composio's.
You need polling triggers faster than managed auth's 15-minute minimum.

verdict.oneLiner: Minutes if your scopes are non-sensitive — 6+ weeks and a paid security audit if you need to read mail.

readyIn.min: 2–3 business days (brand verification only, non-sensitive scopes)
readyIn.worst: 6+ weeks (restricted scopes requiring a tier-3 CASA assessment)

criticalPath.action: Start brand verification and domain ownership verification on day one.
criticalPath.why: Brand verification alone takes 2–3 business days and gates everything else, so it should be running while you build.

criticalPath.action: Pick the narrowest scope that does the job — prefer gmail.send over full mail access.
criticalPath.why: Sensitive scopes clear in about 10 business days; restricted scopes drag you into an annual, paid CASA security assessment. The scope you choose decides which timeline you are on.

criticalPath.action: If you genuinely need restricted scopes, line up a CASA assessor early.
criticalPath.why: The assessment itself runs 2–3 weeks (tier 2) or 4–6 weeks (tier 3) and is billed by a third party, so starting late adds that time to your launch date.

criticalPath.action: Write the scope justification before you submit, not during review.
criticalPath.why: Justifying each requested scope is the most common source of back-and-forth, and requesting scopes the app does not visibly use gets submissions rejected.

beforeApproval.whatWorks: The app works end to end, but only for a small set of test users, and every one of them sees an "unverified app" warning screen before they can continue.
limits: Unverified apps are capped at 100 users.
That 100-user counter cannot be reset — burning it on testing is permanent.
Tokens issued while the app is in testing mode expire after 7 days.
Internal-only Google Workspace apps are exempt from verification entirely.

steps.title: Work out which scopes you actually need
steps.detail: Map each feature to the narrowest scope that supports it. Sending mail needs gmail.send (sensitive). Reading or modifying mail needs gmail.readonly / gmail.modify / mail.google.com (restricted, and far more expensive in time and money).

steps.title: Create the Google Cloud project and configure the OAuth consent screen
steps.detail: In Google Cloud Console, create a project, enable the Gmail API, and fill in the OAuth consent screen: app name, logo, support email, authorised domains and privacy policy URL.
steps.whyHuman: Requires a signed-in Google Cloud account and acceptance of terms.

steps.title: Verify domain ownership
steps.detail: Verify every authorised domain and the redirect URI domain in Google Search Console under the same account that owns the Cloud project.
steps.whyHuman: Requires DNS or registrar access to prove ownership.

steps.title: Submit for brand verification
steps.detail: Submit the consent screen for brand verification, which checks that the logo, display name, URLs and domain ownership honestly represent the app.
steps.whyHuman: Submitting for review is an account action Google ties to a responsible person.

steps.title: Request scope verification with written justification
steps.detail: For each sensitive or restricted scope, explain what the app does with the data and record a demo video showing that exact use. Sensitive scopes are reviewed in about 10 business days.
steps.whyHuman: Requires submitting a review request and a demo video from the owning account.

steps.title: Complete the CASA security assessment (restricted scopes only)
steps.detail: Google's Trust and Safety team tells you when to begin. You engage an independent assessor, pay their fee, and repeat the assessment annually for as long as you use restricted scopes.
steps.whyHuman: Involves a commercial engagement, payment, and giving an assessor access to your environment.

config.redirectUriNotes: Use the exact redirect URI shown in your Composio auth config, and make sure its domain is listed as an authorised domain and verified in Search Console. A mismatch between the registered redirect URI and the one Composio sends is the most common cause of a failed callback.

scopes.name: https://www.googleapis.com/auth/gmail.send
scopes.purpose: Send mail as the user. The cheapest path if you only need to send.

scopes.name: https://www.googleapis.com/auth/gmail.modify
scopes.purpose: Read, label and modify mail, excluding permanent deletion.

scopes.name: https://mail.google.com/
scopes.purpose: Full mailbox access including permanent deletion. Avoid unless genuinely required.

review.requiredWhen: Whenever the app requests sensitive or restricted scopes and is used by anyone outside your own Google Workspace organisation. Internal-only Workspace apps are exempt.
process: Brand verification — checks that logo, display name, URLs and domain ownership represent the app honestly.
Sensitive scope verification — checks that the use of each sensitive scope is neither deceptive nor broader than needed.
Restricted scope verification — the same check at a higher bar, plus a mandatory CASA security assessment.
CASA security assessment — performed by an independent third-party assessor, repeated annually.
review.timeline: Brand verification 2–3 business days; sensitive scope verification about 10 business days; CASA 2–3 weeks (tier 2) or 4–6 weeks (tier 3). Google publishes these as expected times, not guarantees.
review.cost: Verification itself is free. The CASA assessment involves fees payable to the third-party assessor, ranging from $500 to $4,500 USD depending on the app's complexity (Google's own figure, checked 2026-10-20).
review.recurring: Apps using restricted scopes must repeat the CASA security assessment annually.

gotchas.text: The 100-user cap on unverified apps cannot be reset, so every throwaway test account you authorise is gone permanently.
Tokens issued in testing mode expire after 7 days, which looks like a broken refresh flow if you do not know to expect it.
Requesting scopes your app does not visibly use is a common rejection reason — reviewers check the demo video against the scope list.
Choosing mail.google.com when gmail.send would do converts a roughly two-week review into a 6+ week one with a recurring annual audit.
Published timelines are expected completion times, not commitments — plan for them to slip.

composioHandoff: In the Composio dashboard: Create Auth Config → choose the Gmail toolkit + OAuth2.
Register the provider app using the redirect URI Composio shows you, and add that domain to your authorised domains in Google Cloud.
Paste the Client ID and Client Secret from your Google Cloud OAuth client.
Copy the resulting ac_... auth config id and pass it via auth_configs in your session.

claims.text: Composio offers managed OAuth for the Gmail toolkit.
Google requires three types of verification: brand verification (2–3 business days), sensitive scope verification (10 business days), and restricted scope verification.
